Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES September 2, 2021

A Special meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission - Measure A Community
Engagement Workshop - was convened on September 2, 2021 via Zoom. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:35 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent

  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large

Public Comments

  None

Verbal Reports

Director Barnes an overview regarding Measure A. In 2015, the City participated in a Countywide
Park Needs Assessment (CPNA) led by the Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space
District. The purpose of the study was to better understand how to improve, expand and make parks
more accessible so that all communities can thrive. Seventy-five percent (75%) of Los Angeles
County voters approved Measure A in November of 2016, which authorizes dedicated local funding
for park, recreation, and open space projects and their maintenance through an annual special tax
of 1.5 cents per square foot of building floor area on all taxable real property in the County. The Los
Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District (RPOSD) is responsible for implementing
and administering the Los Angeles County Safe, Clean Neighborhood Parks and Beaches Measure
of 2016 (Measure A). Measure A makes funding available to eligible recipients for projects that repair
and upgrade parks and recreational facilities; create new parks; preserve and protect open spaces
and beaches; and support recreational programming. To qualify for funding, Measure A applicants
must conduct community outreach and engagement with the intent to 1) Ensure the applicant’s
community is included in the determination of spending priorities: and 2) Report to the community
how Measure A funds are being applied to projects. This workshop is designed to share background
information regarding Measure A with community members and ultimately result in the development
of a prioritized list of potential park projects to be funded by Measure A. Discussion was held as part

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES September 2, 2021

of the initial CPNA, the Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department hosted a Community
Engagement meeting which resulted in the development of an initial list of projects in 2016, and
subsequent list in 2019, based on the inventory of existing parks, park amenities and their conditions,
as well as park project needs pre-identified by City staff.

In addition, participants were asked to share their ideas for additional park projects they would like
to see in the community. Proposed projects that were noteworthy, but outside of the scope of the
CPNA, were also documented for future consideration. Part of the discussion included sharing a list
of proposed projects and receiving public input with questions and suggestions from both the public
and the Parks Commission following that a Poll was conducted and Commission recommendations
were heard.

The following Projects have been completed since the initial 2015 Priority List:
   Restroom Improvement Project (Rogers, Ashwood, Center, and North)
   Vincent & Darby Park Electrical Upgrades
   Center Park Expansion/ Improvement Project
   Vincent Park Veterans Building Improvements (Roof replacement, interior painting and
  flooring)
   Darby Park Surface Improvements (Walking path)
   Darby Park Dodgers Dream fields (Ballfield upgrades)
   Tennis Court Improvements/Resurfacing (Darby, Rogers, Ash, North, and Vincent Park)
   Ashwood Park Improvement Project including Splash Pad
   Wi-Fi access at Darby, Rogers and Vincent Park

Director Barnes informed attendees that the current allocation funds available is $1.8 million.
Community engagement meetings are one of the requirements that must be met to receive Measure
A funding. This is to ensure that the community is included in the determination of the spending
priorities - that the community has a voice. Another requirement is that the City report how Measure
A funds are being applied to projects. Everyone has a role. Staff’s role includes the identification of
projects that they believe are the most urgent or pressing (11 were identified). Public input is
welcomed. The public’s role is to assist, suggest and help to prioritize the proposed projects. The
Commission will then recommend these projects for City Council’s approval. The purpose of the list
is to assist the City in future park planning, serve as a guide for potential development, serve as a
guide for funding Measure A and other funding mechanisms and it will guide local decisions by both
the Commission and City Council. Projects related to health and safety will have the highest priority.
The general approach for developing the list is centered on health and safety and areas that need
modernization or upgrades, improving of the aesthetic and a general need.

Director Barnes recommended that renovation of restrooms at both Edward Vincent and Darby Park
be a part of the Citywide Park Restroom Improvement Project. Commissioner Fargoso asked
Director Barnes for clarification of new construction as it relates to the sprucing up of current

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES September 2, 2021

maintenance. Director Barnes stated that total renovations have been completed including
construction of a new restroom at North Park. The most recent restroom completed is located at
Rogers Park; the previous restroom was completely demolished and a brand new restroom was
constructed. Intentions for Edward Vincent Park are to also demolish the existing restroom located
near the amphitheater and construct a new one. Commissioner Fragoso expressed his concern with
the term upgrade verses reconstruction. Director Barnes acknowledged and further explained this
will be a total renovation - demolition of existing restrooms both at Edward Vincent and Darby Park
and construction of new restrooms. Commissioner Beck asked with the term demolished is that
demolishing the structure and reframing of the structure including plumbing or simply anything
located within the walls. Director Barnes indicated new construction from the ground up.

The projects will be taken individually. Edward Vincent has three recommendations:

  Upgrade/Refurbish Ball Fields/Turf including fencing, seating, scoreboard.
  Replace Playground Rubber Surfacing (6 sites)
  Renovate Shaded Structure including tables, seating and sinks (Picnic Area).

Rogers Park improvements would include:

  Upgrade/Refurbish Ball Fields/Turf including fencing, seating, scoreboard.
  Replace Signage and Fencing
  Install Fitness Stations (5)

Director Barnes stated other proposed improvements include upgrading the irrigation system at
Edward Vincent Park, and, if approved, phase II of improving the swimming pool complex,
resurfacing/renovation of the pool deck. Lastly, Director Barnes provided information on another
multi-year project. The Security Enhancement Project involves installation of security surveillance
systems at eight (8) parks. Currently Rogers, Ashwood, Center, Siminski and Darby Park all have
security cameras. The remaining sites are Edward Vincent, North and Queen Park. The
recommendation is to install the next camera system at our flagship park - Edward Vincent Park.

Director Barnes informed all that allocation funds are released annually and so by the next meeting
in October 2021 the $1.8 million dollar allocation will have increased. There is an expectation that
another improvement list will develop within the next two weeks.

Director Barnes requested community input regarding the recommended projects. Mr. Aron Rudnick
was thankful for the community engagement workshop, stating he visits Edward Vincent Park four
or five times per week. The park is located four blocks away from him and has been a life line during
this pandemic. Mr. Rudnick expressed concerns about nature, wildlife and trees stating he has a
proposal to assist with his concerns and wanted to know if his proposal could be heard.
Commissioner Denmon answered the Commission would be open to the submission of his proposal
and provided instruction on how to do so. Director Barnes provided Mr. Rudnick with her email

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES September 2, 2021

address sbarnes@cityofinglewood.org. Director Barnes invited Mr. Rudnick to the Passing of the
Golden Shovel NFL Event taking place September 25, 2021 from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at Edward
Vincent Park. The event will include the planting of 56 trees and other activities designed to increase
the park’s tree inventory and beautify the park. Commissioner Beck encourage Mr. Rudnick to inform
friends and colleagues to volunteer and participate in the event as well. Mr. Rudnick stated Edward
Vincent Park is a community park and that he would be delighted to share this opportunity. He
thanked the Commission. Marlon Pascual provided information regarding AADAP, an agency
specializing in substance abuse prevention. Mr. Pascual mentioned that he visits different parks
within the City of Inglewood and he noticed that the District 3 parks - Ashwood, Grevillea Art and
Siminski do not have any no smoking signs and the parks that do signage should be updated to
include no vaping and marijuana use. Teresa Estrada shared a comment that was made by a
constituent. The constituent agreed that speed bumps were needed to stop cars from doing donuts
and also asked that staff replace the net (by the volleyball pit) to stop balls from going in the parking
lot noting it got destroyed by a vehicle fire. Also, let's get those water refill machines like those in the
lobby of Darby Park. Director Barnes responded to the request for the water bottle refill stations
comment stating three weeks prior she reached out to the West Basin Municipal Water District to
inquire about their water bottle filling station program. She indicated they grants to fund the stations
and staff will be looking to add water bottle filling stations…that is in the works. Commissioner
Denmon referenced the importance of upgrading the irrigation system at Edward Vincent Park,
stating the project isn’t as glamorous or something you’ll see every day it maybe a long project but
again it’s a very important project.

Director Barnes requested a poll from the audience, in addition to requesting the opportunity to hold
additional workshops to gather more input from community members. She noted there are 11
projects and asked participants to select their top five.

Chat comment (Ms. IPad) – request to add additional trash cans in the Warren Lane parking located
alongside 67th Street. Stating people eat in cars and throw trash out in that area.

Results from the poll include:
100% - Renovate the restrooms at Edward Vincent Park
78% - Renovate picnic arbor shade structure at Edward Vincent Park
78% - Install camera system at Edward Vincent Park
67% - Renovate the restrooms at Darby Park
56% - Replace the playground surfacing
56% - Refurbishing ballfields at Rogers Park
56% - Replace signage and fencing at Rogers Park
33% - Upgrade the ballfields
33% - Upgrade irrigation system
22% - Install fitness stations at Roger Park
22% - Resurface/Renovate Pool Deck at Edward Vincent

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES September 2, 2021

Director Barnes stated the results will be given at the tentative October 5, 2021 for Commission
consideration and recommendations. Following that, the matter will then be submitted to the Mayor
and City Council for approval.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners Comments

Commissioner Mc Lemore asked who monitors the cameras at the different parks and what is the
cleaning procedure of the fitness equipment?. Is there a certain time it’s cleaned, since a lot of people
are using it? Director Barnes stated the cameras are monitored through the Inglewood Police
Department. Future installation will also include a monitor at Director Barnes’ desk. We’re looking
into contracting out regarding the cleaning of both the fitness and playground equipment.

Director Barnes informed all that the Parks Recreation Commission meets the first Thursday of every
month with a regular meeting time of 6:00 p.m. The agenda has the time of both the regular and
special meetings.

Commissioner Denmon stated this was definitely a very good meeting and he looks forward to the
next meeting where there can be finalizing of some of the projects that were talked about tonight.

Director Barnes commented with the upcoming budget there will be some projects that will be funded
by the general funds. The goal is to not spend general funds if we don’t have to and/or use that
money for other projects. The City has a firm commitment to making sure that we are upgrading our
parks.

Commissioner Denmon stated there is a very big problem at Darby Park. People are using the
parking lots to attend Sofi-Stadium and walking through the park. Is there a way to lock the gates.
Director Barnes responded we are in conversation with the Police Department as well as the Parking
Team for signage, enforcement and citing.

Commissioner Beck commented that he lives adjacent from Darby Park and has experienced the
wonderful new friends that visit Sofi. Commissioner Beck stated there is somewhat of an gray area
using a previous event for example. There was an event this particular Saturday both at Darby Park
and Sofi- Stadium so there was a question of who was actually attending Darby’s event or Sofi‘s.

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 7:24 p.m.
